newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar hints at no more capital controls.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar hints at no more capital controls.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim indicated on Monday that Malaysia had planned no further capital controls following its curbs on foreign exchange swaps.
Asked if there were any further capital controls planned, Anwar told reporters, "Not until today".

On Sunday, Bank Negara Malaysia said it would require local banks beginning from Monday to observe a limit of $2.0 million on outstanding non-commercial related ringgit offer side swap transactions with each foreign customer.
The central bank's move was an effort to reduce speculation that has roiled the ringgit in the past month.
Asked by reporters following a function how the swaps restriction would be monitored, Anwar said there was already a mechanism in place to do so. He did not elaborate.
The ringgit recouped about 300 points against the dollar earlier on Monday following news of the central bank action. At 0415 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.6070/00 to a dollar.
